key_insight: GEBench provides the first benchmark focused on GUI-specific image generation, evaluating models by how well they predict multi-step GUI state transitions and maintain temporal coherence—not just single-frame visual fidelity.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks emphasize general visual quality but do not assess interaction-driven state transitions or temporal consistency in GUI generation; GEBench fills this evaluation gap.
method: Curate multi-step GUI state sequences paired with user instructions and action labels to form interaction-driven test cases.
Treat image-generation models as GUI environments: run action-conditioned rollouts and compare predicted next states to ground truth using state-transition and temporal-coherence metrics.
Provide a standardized evaluation suite and metrics to measure interaction fidelity, action correctness, and long-horizon consistency across models.
impact: Enables researchers and engineers to benchmark and improve models for interactive UI tasks (e.g., automated agents, UI synthesis) by quantifying how well generated GUIs preserve correct state transitions over time.
visual_elements: Timeline of GUI state sequences showing ground-truth frames and predicted frames with arrows marking transitions
Side-by-side comparison grid highlighting changed regions between ground truth and model outputs for each step
Bar/line charts comparing models on metrics like state-transition accuracy and temporal coherence over rollouts
Pipeline diagram: dataset → model-as-environment rollouts → metric computations and leaderboard
paper_title: GEBench: Benchmarking Image Generation Models as GUI Environments
paper_authors: Haodong Li, Jingwei Wu, Quan Sun, Guopeng Li, Juanxi Tian
